annotation.title_clean: The Principle of Double Effect Applied to Ethical Dilemmas of Social Robots
annotation.title_en: The Principle of Double Effect Applied to Ethical Dilemmas of Social Robots
annotation.authors_or_issuer: IOS Press (author not stated in excerpt)
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 290: What Social Robots Can and Should Do (IOS Press)
annotation.summary_en: Abstract of a conference paper applying the principle of double effect to ethical dilemmas of social robots, such as those studied by Winfield and colleagues. It proposes a formal semantics of actions, causes, intentions and utilities, so that permissibility reduces to checking whether a formula is true.
key_provisions_or_claims: Social robots need ethical principles beyond consequentialism.
The principle of double effect sets conditions for acceptable actions with both good and bad consequences.
Proposes a formal semantics based on Pearl and Horty, with actions, causes, intentions and utilities.
Permissibility under double effect reduces to deciding whether a formula is true.
